links.reason: அறத்தறம் மறத்து (verse 4) does say he forgets virtue, and the cause is செல்வச் செருக்கு in line 1, which Kural 32's மறத்தல் leaves unnamed. But the verse is flagged uncertain, and its forgetting is a turn to காமம் and wealth, not the Kural's general ruin.

2867 never mentions the swan chicks; it only has the king speak of கிளைப்பிரிவு. That the chicks' capture is read back as a parting of kin comes from 2875 and the plot, not the Tamil of these two verses.

Naladiyar 17's warning about a woman's spear-like eyes and the staff does not appear in 2661, which shows only the love-god's army routed and garlands falling. A time limit on the women's yielding is imported, so only the shared theme of pleasure is left.

Both verses show women weeping at Civakan's fate, but 1104 only has them say life will go if his beauty fades (போவுடம்பு வாழுயிர் பொன்று). Nothing in it says he is taken to prison, and 2964 has no going to renunciation beyond the sobbing.

Verse 266 has அடிநிழல் of the king who stands in aram, matching Kural 544's அடிதழீஇ நிற்கும் உலகு. It adds the reason in line 1, men wounding one another (ஒருவரை ஒருவர் வாட்ட), so the clinging is a refuge, not just a condition.

Both 704 and 1141 show the same scorn of men's strength (சிறியோன், மலைத்துணை பெருகிக் காட்டும்), so they agree and do not conflict. Whether 1141 comes after the lion's death is not stated in either Tamil text, and 704 is flagged uncertain.

272 promises அடிப்படுத்து the silver mountain's realm and 292 has the same verb, அடிப்படுத்தினன், of the விஞ்சையர் lords, so a prophecy is kept in the same word. The pair shows the conquest as the foretold fruit of the sage's word.

Soolamani 1600 uses நிழல் as a comic mirror that copies the jester (தன்னிழல் தான்செய்வ செய்ய). It says nothing of deeds' consequences, so Kural 208's shadow of ruin is a different use of the word and the moral dimension is imported.

920 only has drink stocked for guests, விருந்தயர்ந்து, and nothing in it speaks of display, rank or alliance. The note's reading of a royal feast as a limit on Kural 81's household hospitality is the marker's, not the Tamil's.
18 does not say how the cure was made, only சித்தம் குழையற்க எனத் தீர்த்து. That it is the spells of 16 at work is a reconstruction, and 16 and 18 are just two items in the patikam's list.

139 is the king's refusal to kill to save himself, said to his mother. 181 is only the grandson ordering a crocodile killed, so there is no claim in 181 to conflict with 139. That he is the heir who forgot the vow rests on plot outside the two verses.

Verse 7 names four kinds of எச்சில் (இந்நான்கு) and verse 8 opens with நால்வகை எச்சிலும், so the later verse depends on the earlier for what it means. It adds what the four bar (ஓதார் உரையார் வளராரே) and the result, மேதைகள் ஆகுறுவார்.

2766 shows hell's torments as the cost of hurting living beings (உயிரைப் பேதுறுத்து), and Siddhar 16 hopes to escape பாழ்நரகு by knowing the breath. Pairing them as a different way out is the marker's construction, since neither verse sets conduct against knowledge.

330 has the minister only ask that the worthy prince be examined and told. The note's Pavachchuthan whose word settles it is not in the verse, and the verse is not about choosing counsellors as Kural 445 is.

205 has the princess take an ஒர் நோன்பு and think how to finish it, and 212 names the vow சக்கரவாளம் and has her keep it. The vow does come to its end, but this is story sequence the graph already records, and the second act is the verse's own.

444 makes allies greater than oneself the chief strength (வன்மையுள் எல்லாம் தலை) and 497 says no support is needed but அஞ்சாமை. 497 is conditional (எண்ணி இடத்தால் செயின்), so it adds a condition to 444 and is not a clean conflict.

1216 has a தெய்வ வாய்மொழி that the youth will win and reign, and 402 foretells that the Kesava will take Ashvagriva's life. That 1216 echoes the same word is not stated, and it rests on the plot identifying the youth with the Kesava.

Both bow the head (இறைஞ்சினள், இறைஞ்சினாள்), but in 230 the man stays in great pain (பெரிய எவ்வம்) and the poem does not say he read the gesture as unreadable. That the Kural's reading is made after the fact is the marker's.
Both verses have him go up a tall mansion (மாடம் ஏறினான்). The repeated climb is only a recurrence in the wedding sequence, and the chapter-framing teaches adds nothing the two verses show.

Both call him Kama, அநங்கனாயினான் and அநங்கனாய், which is a stock figure for a handsome hero. 2358 does not mention a battle and 2425 does not mention the wedding bath, so the note's conquest-then-marriage progression is not in the Tamil.

1339 gives the father's reasons as the marks of a ruler and the saving of her life, and says nothing of the secret union in 1329. That the union already requires the marriage is the note's reading, so the verse is only the next step of the plot.

1099 gives the bride நீரொடு before the fire as god (கடவுளாக), which fits the rite behind கடி. Naladiyar 56 says nothing of rite or fire, only of the husband's inability to put the wife away, and 1099 does not say that the gift causes that duty.

909 says the game became a cause of sorrow (இன்பக் காரணம்... துன்பக் காரணம்), which is near the quatrain's pain in pleasure. But Gunamalai only weeps for her friend and does not turn from pleasure, so the renunciation frame is imported.

139 is the king's refusal and 142 is the mother's answer offering a flour cock (கோழியை மாவிற் செய்து), so 142 gives a way round and is not an opposed claim. 144 supports the test of whether a likeness counts, which fits develops better than tension.

Both are vows that wish a base lot on the speaker if he fails (இல்லாளை அஞ்சி... in 2319; the loss of wife and friends in Purananuru 71), so the form is shared. But the claim that the vow is shown 'unfulfilled' for Purananuru's speaker is not shown by either text.

162 has the cloud vanish and விரத்தி arise, a sudden turn on sight of impermanence, which the quatrain's list names. The epic side's 'reasoned choice' is wrong, since the verse shows no reasoning, and it mostly illustrates the quatrain.

Both use the swan on the Ganges, but 1017 makes it a constant lover and 1385 a hen left at a dry pool (பெடை... வறுஞ்சுனை). The two do not state incompatible claims, and that the second turns the first against Civakan is the marker's reading.

144 says the king shrinks from a likeness of life as it is like killing (உயிர்க்கொலை போலும்), and 146 has the flour cock cry and fall so that he drops the sword and melts (உருகினானே). The later verse bears out the earlier misgiving in the scene.

1280 has victors not scorn the one who blinks (இமைப்பினும் இகழ்ந்தெறிதல் செய்யார்), against Kural 775's blink as flight. It limits the strict rule with mercy on the loser, and the couplet in turn shows the reflex the epic spares.

1469 has the eight qualities (எண்குணன், printed வெண்குணன்) seized from souls by karma, and Tirumanthiram 444 gives them to Siva. These assign them to different holders and do not make incompatible claims, so there is no tension, only a shared word.
links.text_issue: line 4 வெண்குணனும் is probably எண்குணனும்; sense uncertain

links.reason: 1037 has her draw a circle praying the union come about, and 1039 has the parrot bring his message, so the second answers the first in the plot. That the circle is replaced by news is the note's reading, since the circle's result is never stated.

Innaa Narpathu 39 counts a poet's not being sent off after the gift as painful (கொடுத்த விடாமை கவிக்கின்னா), and Purananuru 101 shows the late gift and Avvai's calm. The fit is with the delay of the gift, not a poet who is held back after receiving it.

1327 has Civakan settle that Padumai is mortal by signs (மாலை வாடின, வாள்கண் இமைத்தன), and 1473 has him wonder whether Kemasari is தாக்கணங்கு or a mortal. It is the same doubt, not a qualification, and the contrast of coolness against wonder is the note's.

124 spares the woman because women are not fit to be killed (மாதரார் வதையினுக்குரியரல்லர்) and the sword is too high for the base, not because life is dear. Kural 327 pairs with that, but the husband's rage is not in the verse.

1143 has Arikethu marvel at the youth who tore the lion (கீறி), which refers back to 723's tearing. But it was Arikethu who played the lion at 697, which is not in either verse, so the teaches rests on the plot.
363 lists ஐம்புலம் மடக்கி among a numbered scheme, and Kural 126 has ஐந்தடக்கல். The tortoise and the reward over seven births belong only to the Kural, so this is a shared idea, not a development.

2875 has the elder warn that those who cage birds will be parted from their kin (தங்கிளையின் நீங்கிப் போவர்), and 2880 has the prince, having heard dharma, free the cygnet. The deed answers the rebuke within a few verses.

520 has Dharan promise to return the dead companions in a blink (இமைப்பினுள் மறித்தே தருகுவன்), and 582 has them alive, laughing that it was a play (நாடகம்). The promise is kept and the deaths are shown as staged.

225 has the dream read as a son and fortune, and 2417 has women bless him with ghee to be lord with Fortune (திருவோடு). A blessing in a rite is not the dream's fulfilment, so the step by step claim goes beyond the Tamil.

856 has கேவலக் கிழவன் only in a simile for the festival crowd, and Tirumanthiram 2162's kevala is the soul's first state with anava. They are different technical senses of one word, so there is no claim of the verse to be in tension.

78 has the king go to the forest and the sons leave the realm (மன்னன்போய் வனமடைந்து). The verse gives no impermanence for the quatrain's list of kings carried off, so it only illustrates renunciation, and that gain is imported.

1124 recalls that Sunandai had borne many children who died (செதுமகப் பலவும் பெற்று), then the ascetic came, and 325 has Kantukkatan leave his dead son and take the child. It supplies background, but that the exchange answers a prepared grief is the note's reading.

466's women ask him to come in a dream and அருளி, which pairs with Kural 1214's dream bringing the man who gives no grace (நல்காரை). The Kural does not say he was once hers, so the couplet's situation is overstated, though the extension to strangers is real.
